title: shipped a small browser game in 4 days with claude code, zero image gen, everything is drawn in code
author: Mindless-Document-41
selftext:
river madness: you paddle a canoe down an endless river, swipe on each side of the boat to steer. one life

built it in my spare time. the idea and sketches were mine (literally paper notes on mechanics and level structure), claude code wrote all the godot 4 code. i had it draw everything in code instead of using image gen, so the boats, crocs, rocks and water are all just shapes. web build ended up around 10mb which is pretty nice

biggest unlock for me was playtesting on my phone after every iteration, dumping everything that felt off into a list and handing it right back. took like 8 rounds before i shipped. it also wrote a bot that plays the game and runs \~250 checks after every change, honestly saved me from a ton of regressions i never would've caught

sounds are the only part with no ai, recorded them on my synth

free in the browser: [https://kencha.games/river-madness/](https://kencha.games/river-madness/)

so here's where i'm stuck. most people play it once and never come back the next day. what moved the needle for you guys on getting people to return? also if you've gone the code-drawn route instead of image gen, does this look hold up or is it too plain? lmk, tbh any feedback helps

comments.author: Early_Flamingo5337
comments.body: Didn't alva majo had a game with exactly that name?

replies.author: Mindless-Document-41
replies.body: oh interesting, didn't know that! i searched before naming it and couldn't find anything, do you have a link? if it's the same name i'd def want to know

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: And it is also about ships and pretty similar pov

replies.author: Mindless-Document-41
replies.body: ahh you mean shipped! just checked it out, that's an 8 player naval brawler with hex islands, pretty different from mine. "shipped" in my title just means i launched it lol

replies.author: Early_Flamingo5337
replies.body: My mistake there hahahahaha, I just saw the images and first word and I got totally confused

replies.author: Mindless-Document-41
replies.body: haha all good, honestly a fair mixup. thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: BrotherMoy
comments.body: You said the biggest unlock for you was playtesting on your phone after every iteration. How were you able to do this, especially with a Godot project? Right now, unless I have Claude make an html file, I won't be able to iterate on anything directly with my phone. This looks really good and considering it's made with Godot, can be ported as a mobile app pretty easily.

replies.author: Mindless-Document-41
replies.body: Thanks, appreciate it! Yeah, it's basically the html route, just automated. Claude Code set up the Godot web export once and serves it from my Mac on my home wifi, so I open that link in Chrome or Safari on my phone. Nothing installed. Every time it changes something it re-exports and I just refresh the page, and it's the same Godot project the whole time, no separate html version to keep in sync. And agreed on the app, Android is next.

replies.author: BrotherMoy
replies.body: Wow I didn't think of this! Do you find the html version of the game runs like a regular mobile app? I feel like it would be annoying to see the address bar, and the aspect ratio issues with scrolling would be a pain too no?

replies.author: Mindless-Document-41
replies.body: Honestly for playtesting it's close enough, but not quite like a real app. The address bar does show up in Safari and Chrome, and I just live with it while testing. Aspect ratio wasn't a big deal since Godot's "expand" stretch mode handles different phones pretty well, and the game canvas doesn't scroll the page. The things that actually bit me were audio on iOS (it needs a tap before it plays) and performance on cheaper Android phones in Chrome, which took some tuning. For the real release I'd do a proper Android build anyway.
